newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end down sharply in data fallout.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end down sharply in data fallout.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended sharply lower after a session of steep losses on strong U.S. economic data.

June Treasury bond futures slid through key support in the upper 106-00 handle to post a session low at 106-12/32, a fresh seven-month low. Strong core producer prices for March and an upward revision to February retail sales sent debt prices into a tailspin as players took it as more evidence the Fed will raise interest rates in May.
U.S. March PPI fell 0.1 pct overall and rose 0.4 percent in the core rate versus forecasts for unchanged and up 0.1 pct.
March retail sales rose 0.2 pct and 0.5 pct ex-autos versus respective forecasts for up 0.6 pct and up 0.4 pct. Feb retail sales were revised to up 1.5 pct from up 0.8 pct.
June T-bonds plumbed their lows all afternoon, coming quite close to a full point of losses. Support at the session low of 106-12/32 held, with small buying into the close, traders said.
September Eurodollars slid to 93.635, the lowest price since April 1 when the contract slid to 93.63. Below there, September 1996 lows loom.
As for further Eurodollar support: "It's hard to say," one broker said. "We're getting into some uncharted territory."
For now, support rests at 93.60 to 62 in September Euros and at 93.24-25 in December, he said.
Traders said the tone would remain defensive heading into next week's March consumer price report.
"We saw a lot of selling today, we never really recovered and we gradually traded lower throughout the day," said Don Pullen, bond trading floor manager for ED and F Man.

"There was a little slight bounce late but market sentiment remains bearish," he said. A strong core CPI rate next Tuesday would push the long bond yield to 7.25 percent, taking June T-bonds another point lower, Pullen said.
Pullen said the sentiment was still to sell rallies.

Others agreed, saying short-covering bounces may develop early next week, but upticks should be sold. One Eurodollar futures trader said the fact that short-covering failed to materialize late Friday in the short end shows that market sentiment was still very soft.
"Until the market tells you otherwise, you continue to sell it," he said. "I think the market is saying that 25 basis points wasn't enough and there'll be more down the rode."
At the close, June T-bonds were down 23/32 at 106-20/32, notes were down 13/32 at 105-08/32, munis lost 26/32 to 111-20/32, Sep bills fell 0.050 to 94.250, Sept Euros fell 0.065 to 93.665.
